reflection: Volume-surge signals (AAPL vs NVDA, NVDA alone, QQQ alone) helped in 2023 and 2025 but missed in 2022 and 2024, and most gains are small and Random Forest-only, so none has cleared the team bar. The misses look driven by a few extreme volume spikes and by ignoring market direction, while smoothing and longer baselines did not fix them. Next I will compress extreme spikes with a log transform, test whether overnight QQQ gaps and range surges carry new peer information, and pair range-based Apple/MSFT measures with volume signals.

lessons.name: nvda_volume_surge_smooth
lessons.lesson: Smoothing NVDA volume over 5 days lost the sharp same-day spike signal and missed badly in 2024, so averaging the volume did not help.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_surge_smooth_minus_qqq
lessons.lesson: Replacing the daily volume ratios with 5-day averages removed the timing information and the result flipped sign across years, so it was rejected.

lessons.name: peer_range_ratio_msft_nvda
lessons.lesson: The MSFT-to-NVDA range ratio helped in three years and both models, but its gain is too small to trust and it did not help in 2024.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_change_3d
lessons.lesson: A 3-day percent change in AAPL volume is noisy and lacks a direction or baseline, so it helped in only two years and neither model.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_nvda
lessons.lesson: The relative AAPL-minus-NVDA volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but missed in 2022 and 2024, probably because the raw ratio is driven by extreme spikes.

lessons.name: aapl_range_surge
lessons.lesson: The Apple range surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but its gain is tiny and it overlaps with AAPL_daily_range, so it carries little independent information.

factors.name: nvda_volume_surge_log
factors.hypothesis: The parent missed in 2022 and 2024 probably because a few extreme NVDA volume spikes dominate the linear scale; a log transform compresses those spikes so the signal reflects typical surges rather than outliers.

factors.name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_nvda_log
factors.hypothesis: The parent's gap is driven by extreme ratio spikes in either stock; taking logs of each ratio before subtracting makes the relative surge symmetric and less dominated by one-day outliers, which may fix the 2022 and 2024 misses.

factors.name: qqq_overnight_gap_1d
factors.hypothesis: The overnight gap in QQQ reflects news that arrives before the open and can lead Apple's next-day move; it is a QQQ-based measure, unlike the rejected Apple overnight gap.

factors.name: qqq_range_surge
factors.hypothesis: A same-day jump in the market's range relative to its own 20-day norm signals a shift in market regime that a plain 10-day range average did not capture.

factors.name: aapl_msft_range_ratio
factors.hypothesis: Pairing the MSFT-NVDA range ratio with Apple's range relative to MSFT isolates whether Apple itself is more volatile than its megacap peer, which may sharpen the market-level range signal.

factors.name: aapl_range_volatility_10d
factors.hypothesis: Pairing NVDA's volume surge with the variability of Apple's own daily range tests whether peer volume spikes matter more when Apple's intraday risk is already elevated.
